Key Points to be Considered While Resubmitting Your Dissertation

Tagged: Dissertation Writing

Share this:

  • Facebook
  • Twitter
  • LinkedIn

Students may be asked to rework and resubmit dissertation if they do not follow university recommendations, have unintended plagiarism, the research methodology is not best suited for the study, the arguments are weak, have errors in the format and grammar or if there are ethical concerns during data collection. While students may feel discouraged from reworking and resubmitting their dissertations, the following key points may be beneficial for dissertation resubmission:

  1. Seek and review the feedback

    2. Read and comprehend the feedback given to you by your supervisor or committee members. Determine which sections need to be improved or clarified.

  2. Understand the prerequisites

    3. Understand the dissertation guidelines and prerequisites for resubmitting a dissertation. Make sure you understand what changes are expected, as well as any additional documentation or explanations that may be required.
    The prerequisites may vary depending on the discipline- those for biological and life sciences is significantly different from that for economics, arts, or engineering.

  3. Develop a plan

    4. Create a detailed plan to address the feedback. Divide the activities into manageable tasks and prioritise them based on the importance of the adjustments that must be made. Create a timetable to help you stay organized and reach the resubmission date.

  4. Revise the content

    5. Concentrate on the specific areas of improvement identified in the feedback. Revise and reorganize your dissertation chapters to ensure the information is correct, logical, and well-structured. You can get the dissertation checked and corrected for plagiarism to ensure that there is no unintended plagiarism. Where necessary, supplement your arguments with further evidence or examples. Ensure the reworked dissertation is in accordance with the dissertation plan.

  5. Consider the research methodology and data analysis

    6. If you have doubts about your methodology or data analysis, reconsider your research methodology. Provide a complete explanation of your process, address any constraints, and ensure that your data analysis adheres to best practices in your discipline.

  6. Proofread for any errors and make necessary adjustments

    7. Proofread your dissertation thoroughly to ensure that there are no grammatical mistakes, typos, or formatting issues. Examine the overall coherence and flow of the content and make any necessary changes for clarity and conciseness.

    Check the uniformity and accuracy of your citations and references. Ensure you have cited all sources properly and adopted the required citation style.

  7. Include additional research

    8. A dissertation resubmission may be mandated if the research is insufficient. If the feedback indicates that additional study or supporting evidence is required, make sure to include the appropriate sources and elaborate on the current literature review or statistical analysis.

  8. Seek external feedback

    9. Consider sharing your revised work with trusted mentors or peers who can offer constructive comments. Their viewpoints may aid in identifying areas for improvement or provide helpful insights. You can consider seeking the help of trusted dissertation help who will help clear doubts and revise your dissertation.

  9. Follow the guidelines for dissertation resubmission

    10. Acquaint yourself with the resubmission guidelines provided by your institution or programmer. Include all essential papers, adhere to the prescribed format, and fulfil the resubmission deadline. The length and format of a dissertation may differ depending on the discipline.
    A dissertation’s length may also vary depending on whether it is empirical or non-empirical. For more guidance, check out our blog on ‘What is the length of empirical & non-empirical dissertations?’

    Dissertation resubmission, also called resit dissertation, provides an opportunity to improve the quality of the dissertation. Taking feedback constructively, paying attention to details and approaching the revisions with a positive attitude can significantly improve the quality of your dissertation.
